title: assurance-scripts-for-sales-and-cse
content:
Purpose: quick, field-ready scripts and competitive angles for GTM and CSE to talk about Redwood's assurance posture (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA), data handling guarantees, and audit-log language. This is a lightweight playbook: copyable lines, objection responses, and short contract-friendly phrasing. NOT final legal language — coordinate with legal when moving to proposals.

Audience: Sales AE/SDR, Customer Success Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Legal pre-sales reviewers.

High-level positioning (one-liner for intro):
- We treat inference as a first-class production service — we combine industry-standard controls (SOC2/ISO) with operational controls built for low-latency LLM serving and an audit log model that surfaces per-request lineage for compliance reviews.

Elevator scripts (30s / 90s):
- 30s: "We're Redwood Inference — a production-first inference platform. For regulated customers, we offer SOC2 and ISO-aligned controls, optional HIPAA handling for covered workloads, and granular audit logs that make it easy to demonstrate who accessed what model and when."
- 90s: "Many teams wrestle with how to prove their model access and data flow during audits. Redwood provides (1) a verified set of security controls aligned to SOC2/ISO, (2) private deployment options and KMS integrations for sensitive data, and (3) immutable, tamper-evident audit logs that map requests to model versions and routing decisions. That combination reduces evidence collection time and avoids costly ingestion or proxying workarounds."

Key claims + plain-language backup (for AE cheat-sheet):
- Claim: SOC2 Type II in-scope for hosted API operations.
  Backup: We undergo an annual Type II audit covering logical access, change management, incident response and availability controls. We can provide the SOC2 report under NDA.
- Claim: ISO 27001-aligned controls for our control plane and engineering processes.
  Backup: We are mapping our policies and evidence to ISO clauses; we publish an ISO alignment summary for enterprise review.
- Claim: HIPAA-ready support for covered PHI workflows (private deployments + BAA).
  Backup: For customers with PHI, we offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) and a BAA that limits where and how data is processed; we recommend on-prem or Private for highest assurance.
- Claim: Per-request audit trails with model version, route, token metadata and operation latency.
  Backup: Audit logs can be exported to customer SIEMs or delivered via S3/Cloud Storage with configurable retention and cryptographic hashing for tamper-evidence.

Suggested audit-log language (draft copy for contracts / security questionnaires):
- "Redwood Inference maintains comprehensive request-level logs for inference traffic. Each log record includes a timestamp, the model identifier and version, the tenant or workspace ID, routing decisions (region/model-variant), request and response size, and processing latency. Logs are retained according to the customer agreement and can be delivered via secure export (S3/GCS) or streamed to the customer's logging endpoint. Upon request, Redwood can provide hash-signed samples of logs for integrity verification."

Data handling / privacy messaging (short forms):
- Minimal exposure script: "We do not use customer inference data to improve public models. Customer data is isolated per workspace; for private deployments data never leaves your environment unless you explicitly enable export."
- Encryption script: "All data in transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS1.3. At rest, platform-managed keys are AES-256; customers can bring their own keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private deployments."
- Retention script: "Default retention is X days for logs and Y days for request traces — configurable in your contract. For sensitive workloads, we support reduced retention or immediate purge flows implemented through our data governance APIs."

Competitive angles (how to frame differences versus common alternatives):
- Vs. general cloud AI endpoints: 
  Angle: cloud vendors provide compute but not inference-first observability and audit semantics. Redwood combines optimized serving with direct, request-centric audit trails that map to model lineage — meaning auditors can connect a specific output to the exact model build and routing decision.
- Vs. single-tenant inference vendors: 
  Angle: single-tenant vendors may offer isolation but often lack mature SLO-backed routing, autoscaling, and integrated SOC2/ISO evidence. Redwood's Dedicated + Private options give isolation without losing our operational tooling (rollouts, fallback policies, cost telemetry).
- Vs. open-source self-hosting: 
  Angle: self-hosting gives control but requires months of engineering to create defensible controls (change management, incident response, automated log integrity). Redwood provides that operational maturity out of the box, including templates and evidence collectors for auditors.

Common objections and suggested rebuttals (copyable):
- Objection: "We need a BAA for HIPAA."
  Rebuttal: "We sign BAAs for covered PHI workflows. For the strongest assurance, we recommend Private deployments or Dedicated capacity so keys and network controls stay under your control. I can loop in Legal to start the BAA discussion and share our BAA template."
- Objection: "Can auditors see raw request data?"
  Rebuttal: "We typically deliver redacted or hashed samples for external review; full raw request export is available for Private/Dedicated customers subject to contract terms. For hosted customers we can provide scoped samples and our SOC2 report evidence."
- Objection: "How do you prevent log tampering?"
  Rebuttal: "We support write-once export to customer-owned S3/GCS plus cryptographic hashing and sequencing metadata for tamper-evidence. For the highest assurance we can stream logs directly to your SIEM."

CSE playbook for a security review call (step-by-step):
1) Pre-call prep: gather customer environment (cloud provider, SIEM, expected retention, BAA requirement). Reference ticket JIRA:GTMP-3421 if there's a prior compliance ask.
2) Opening (2 minutes): articulate scope: "We will cover SOC2/ISO posture, data flow for your planned integration, audit log exports, and deployment options for PHI."
3) Walk the data flow diagram (3–5 min): map request from customer app -> Redwood API / Private endpoint -> serving runtime -> model variant -> response and logging. Highlight where data is encrypted, where keys can be customer-managed, and where logs land.
4) Show concrete artifacts (5–10 min): SOC2 summary (redacted) + sample audit log schema + export demo (S3 stream or SIEM connection).
5) Live Q&A: capture any legal/technical asks and convert to clear next steps (e.g., need SOC2 report NDA, BAA review, KMS integration runbook).

Quick repo of copy-paste lines for emails/slack replies:
- Short: "We maintain SOC2 controls and can share the Type II report under NDA. For PHI, we offer Private deployments + BAA. Audit logs include model id, version, tenant id, timestamps and routing metadata and can be streamed to your SIEM."
- Technical: "Logs are JSON lines with fields: ts, request_id, tenant_id, model_id, model_version, route, latency_ms, req_size, resp_size. Exports support S3/GCS and streaming endpoints; retention is contract-configurable."

Demo checklist for audit-log export (CSE):
- Verify customer SIEM endpoint and auth method.
- Prepare sample log exports (last 24h) with hashed request bodies.
- Show sequencing/hash verification step.
- Demonstrate model-version field and how rollouts appear in logs.

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Ask Legal for final approved audit-log sample text for contracts (action: Maya -> Legal).
- Confirm standard retention defaults (X/Y) with infra (action: Ethan).
- Prepare a small canned SIEM connector demo video for field enablement (action: Sofia).
- Reconcile wording with SOC2 report extract and ISO alignment doc (linked in confluence).

Appendix: raw examples (copy these into proposals or email threads as needed)
- Audit log example line (redacted): { ts: "2026-02-10T14:22:05Z", request_id: "r-8b2f", tenant_id: "acme-corp", model_id: "gptx-13b", model_version: "v2026-02-01", route: "us-west-2-fallback", latency_ms: 42, req_bytes: 512, resp_bytes: 1024 }
- Contract-friendly sentence for inclusion: "Provider will maintain per-request audit logs that include request identifiers, model identifier and version, tenant identifier, routing decisions, and timestamps; such logs will be made available to Customer under the terms of this agreement subject to data protection constraints."

Status / next steps: incorporate Legal's approved language and produce a short 1-pager for AEs. Recommend an enablement session (30 min) with Sales + CSE to review scripts and demo checklist.

-- end of draft --

Notes: informal, some placeholders (X/Y retention) intentionally left so Legal/Infra can confirm defaults. This file is a working doc; it should be kept in Drive as the single source-of-truth for field messaging until we produce a finalized playbook.
